name: CRAFT
author: Hannu Rummukainen (for Black Legend Ltd)

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga AMOS Factory, CRAFT archive, retrieved 2026-07-26.
provenance.note: Recovered rather than found. The archive ships no .Lib at all -- only a DMS disk image whose contents are an Installer and seven opaque Data blobs. Decompressing the DMS (xdms) and reading the disk gave those blobs, and Data0 turned out to be the library itself behind an eight-byte prefix: HUNK_HEADER sits at offset 8 and the token table parses cleanly from there. The other five packed blobs are now unpacked too, by src/cli/craftx.ts over src/amiga/solaris.ts -- the installer's container is [total:4] then [path\0][size:2] until the sizes add up, then one stream tagged \SOLARIS/, which is the in-house packer of the Finnish house that built the disk (Solaris_Logo.iff is on it). That decruncher was read out of the Installer, itself a compiled AMOS program, at hunk 1 $cce6..$cdac. Data6 is the only blob still unread: a music module, 'craft.jol' by Janne Leinonen. Everything vendored here can be reproduced from the archive by running craftx.
provenance.redistribution: Commercial: published by Black Legend Ltd. Redistribution terms unverified. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: 168 token entries, 138 of them named, over eight groups with little to do with each other: string handling (`up case$`, `flip case$`, `bw instr`, `str scramble$`), a LOGO turtle of 33 keywords driven either one at a time or by a command string through `Tr Exec`, a `dr *` directory scanner over AmigaDOS FileInfoBlocks, palettes held in memory banks, `Fr Mandelbrot` and `Fr Julia`, Workbench and CLI access, six memory queries, and hardware pokes down to `Y Beam` and `Guru Meditation`. It carries no library-name string at all, so nothing in it opens a library: whatever `Open Workbench` and `Sys Request` reach, they reach through a base AMOS already holds. Burton's AMOS Extensions List places it at slot 18, and the disk's own examples confirm the author -- 'Turtle spiral by Hannu Rummukainen' heads one of them. DOCUMENTATION EXISTS AND IS NOW READABLE: CRAFT_Help.AMOS is a hypertext reader by Janne Kalliola whose bank 1 holds 42,874 bytes of plain text, one entry per keyword with syntax and parameter ranges, indexed by 139 DATA statements naming 138 topics. It is where facts like Fr Julia's fixed point come from -- 'multiplying their real values by 8192'. Forty example programs came out of the same disk (fourteen Turtle, seven Fractals, five Colours, plus Token_List, Dir_List, Guru_Alert, Get_Preferences, Info&AvailMem, Priority&Multitasking), which for a library with no manual page per argument order is the better oracle of the two. NOTE THE HELP COVERS A COMPANION TOO: nine of its topics are an `St *` group -- st load, st play, st stop, st pause, st voice, st channel, st vumeter speed, st base, st version -- and none of those is in this token table. They belong to MusiCRAFT, a separate extension whose table stub survives in AMOSTools as AMOSPro_MusiCRAFT.Lib and whose binary is not held here; the disk's Sample_Demo, Toggle_Voice and Vumeter_Demo examples use it, not this library. Accessories/ holds two builds of four programs, AMOS 1.3 from Data1 and AMOS Pro from Data4, kept side by side with a .Data4 suffix. PALETTE BANKS ARE UNDOCUMENTED IN THEIR ONE IMPORTANT DETAIL: the help describes the eleven keywords but never the record they share. Routines 84 and 94 have it, and status.ts cites the addresses -- the eight-byte bank name "Palettes", then 32 words per palette, and a word of $FFFF meaning ABSENT rather than black. That marker is core AMOS's own: PalRout skips $FFFF, which is what lets a masked palette be installed by handing over all 32 words and letting the gaps fall through, and it is why the help can promise that a deleted colour "won't be changed" on the way back in without ever saying how. The same rule cuts the other way twice, in ways nothing documents: a masked Pal To Bank DELETES the bank slots it excludes rather than leaving them, and a masked Pal Swap Bank erases the bank colours it did not swap, because its return leg is masked the same way as its outward one. Two more asymmetries, both between routines that look like a matched pair: =Pal Red admits colour registers 0..63 and reads 32..63 as Extra Half Brite (`lsr.w #1 / andi.w #$777`, and it never asks whether the screen IS half-brite) where Set Red stops at 32; and Pal To Bank's three-argument trampoline tests for AMOS's omitted-parameter marker and will create a bank, where its two-argument one does not and will not.
